data.title: GTA 6 first post-launch update: Staggered PS5 rollout explained
data.description:
Is your GTA 6 update ready? Rockstar Games has started rolling out the first post-launch patch for Grand Theft Auto VI on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S today. The patch is version 01.002.002 on PS5 and 1.0.2.2 on Xbox, and Rockstar has not said what it changes.


How big is the update?

A well-known Rockstar dataminer reports it is 603.8 MB on PS5 and 1.6 GB on Xbox Series X|S. The small size suggests a fix-focused patch and not a major content drop, though that is an inference.


When will PS5 players get it?

The PS5 rollout is staggered in three waves to avoid overloading servers. About 33% of players get it at the start, about 66% roughly three hours later, and everyone about six hours after the rollout began. If it has not appeared yet, wait and check again later. Xbox players could download it at launch.

Are there patch notes?

Not yet. Rockstar has not released notes for this update as of publication. Reports expect fixes for bugs seen since launch, but that is unconfirmed. Rockstar’s support site is the place to watch for official notes.

What bugs might it address?

Players have reported glitches such as characters falling through the map, getting stuck and odd vehicle behavior. One Xbox-only glitch uses Quick Resume to unlock the framerate, which speeds up gameplay and makes it unplayable. GTA 6 Players have also found exploits that break progression and unlock a first-person mode. Whether the patch fixes any of these has not been confirmed.

Why does it matter?

It is the first patch since launch, and the rollout shows the scale of demand. Staggered releases are a way to keep console networks stable.

What is not confirmed?

The contents of the update, its effect on bugs and the exact rollout timing are unconfirmed. Size and version details come from dataminers and may change.

data.title: 2 states sue SpaceX over Grok’s alarming AI abuse images
data.description:
Elon Musk’s SpaceX is facing legal action from two states over its artificial intelligence model Grok. Virginia and Oregon filed lawsuits in state courts on Monday, November 23, accusing SpaceX Super Intelligence Corp. of profiting from a Grok feature that can produce child sexual abuse material and other nonconsensual sexual images from real photographs, all while failing to put proper safeguards in place to stop it.


Several state attorneys general have announced investigations into Grok over similar concerns in recent months, but Virginia and Oregon are the first states to take the company to court. The filings mark a significant escalation in scrutiny of the chatbot, which Musk distributes through his social media platform X.


What the lawsuits claim

The two cases were brought under state consumer protection laws. The first was filed by Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones, and the second was filed by Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield as a separate but similar action. Both seek damages, financial penalties and court orders requiring the company to stop violating state law.

The complaints accuse SpaceX of misleading consumers about Grok’s safety while promoting its “spicy mode.” According to the lawsuits, the feature lets users take an existing photo of a person and turn it into a sexual or nude image or video.

Virginia’s complaint points to research from the Center for Countering Digital Hate, which estimated that Grok generated and posted millions of sexualized images on X between December 2025 and January 2026. More than 20,000 of those images depicted children, according to the study.

SpaceX did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Reuters outside of business hours.

States step up as tech watchdogs

The lawsuits are part of a growing wave of legal action by states against social media and AI companies over harm they say those businesses have caused residents. The cases could test how far states can go in holding AI developers accountable.

Speaking with Reuters ahead of the filings, Jones said state attorneys general have become a key regulatory force in the tech industry, particularly when it comes to artificial intelligence. He noted that AI has faced little oversight at the federal level so far and said attorneys general have stepped in to fill that gap.

Grok’s mounting legal troubles

The state cases add to a long list of legal challenges for the company. SpaceX is already facing more than a dozen lawsuits from individuals who say Grok was used to create nonconsensual sexual images of them, either as minors or as adults.

Across the Atlantic, British lawmaker Jess Asato is suing SpaceX after Grok users generated sexualized images of her. The company has denied her claims, arguing that content that is clearly fictional and created by AI cannot violate a person’s right to privacy.

In January, xAI, the company behind Grok, said it had restricted image editing in the tool and blocked users from generating images of people in revealing clothing in places where doing so is illegal. SpaceX acquired xAI in February and rebranded its AI division as SpaceX Super Intelligence in October.

Even after those changes, a Reuters investigation in early February found that Grok continued to produce sexualized images of people even when users explicitly said the subjects had not given consent. The company did not respond to detailed questions from Reuters about the findings.

SpaceX has also gone on the offensive against some users. The company is suing at least two people in the U.S. whom it accuses of misusing Grok to create child sexual abuse material.

This article was originally reported by Reuters.

data.title: Fortnite Treasure Hours schedule: Start times for every region
data.description:
Want a shot at Fortnite’s rarest rewards? Treasure Hours return today, with two sessions that raise drop rates for the Pirate Shop Access token, the Golden Hatsune Miku outfit and the weekly vehicle and decal. One report calls it the last chance to grab the golden Miku skin.


When are the sessions?

The first runs 11 a.m. to 1 p.m. Pacific, or 2 to 4 p.m. Eastern. The second runs 6 to 8 p.m. Pacific, or 9 to 11 p.m. Eastern. In the UK, they start at 7 p.m. and 2 a.m., and in Central Europe at 8 p.m. and 3 a.m. In India, Japan and Australia, both sessions fall on Nov. 22. Central time starts at 1 and 8 p.m., and Mountain time at noon and 7 p.m.


What are the drop rates?

The Pirate Token normally drops about 1 in 137,500 per Treasure Hunt Chest. The first session lifts that to roughly 1 in 91,667, and the second doubles it to 1 in 68,750. The Golden Miku outfit goes from 1 in 1,562,500 to about 1 in 208,333, a 7.5 times boost, though one report says the second session raises it further. The weekly vehicle and decal improves from 1 in 7,813 to about 1 in 781.

What else changes?

Every player starts with the Leekcapper and a Self-Revive Device. Fortune Sprites reveal nearby chests, while Cursed Sprites raise the odds of rarer variants at the cost of water damage. Both appear more often.

Treasure Hours are landing soon – 2 PM ET | 7 PM UTC⁣

🕘 Second round starts at 9 PM ET | Sunday, 2 AM UTC

— Fortnite (@Fortnite) November 21, 2026

How can you improve your chances?

The token comes only from Treasure Hunt Chests. Land near several chests, use Fortune Sprites to find more and open as many as you can. A token found by one player is shared with the squad, so playing with friends helps.

Why are some players frustrated?

European and Asian players must stay up past midnight for the second session, which has the best odds. Epic has not responded to the complaints. Even at double odds, the token is very unlikely, so staying up until dawn is not worth it.

What comes next?

The Treasure Hunters mini-season ends Dec. 5, so only a few Saturday events remain. Epic hinted rates may be higher in future, but nothing is announced.

What is not confirmed?

Reports differ on the Miku boost during the second session. Epic has not announced a special incentive tied to GTA 6 or details on the Leekcapper’s stats.

data.title: Samsung’s $7 billion AI move could reshape everyday tech
data.description:
Samsung could be preparing a major expansion into the infrastructure powering artificial intelligence, with a reported interest in acquiring a U.S. company valued at approximately $7 billion.


The South Korean technology giant, best known for its smartphones, televisions and household electronics, is reportedly in discussions to acquire Modine Manufacturing, a Wisconsin-based company specializing in heating and cooling equipment for data centers.


The companies could reach an agreement within weeks. However, negotiations remain ongoing, and there is no guarantee that a transaction will be completed.

The potential acquisition reflects a growing challenge facing the technology industry as artificial intelligence becomes more widely used: keeping increasingly powerful computer systems cool without dramatically increasing energy consumption.

Data centers provide the computing capacity behind cloud storage, online applications, AI assistants and many digital services Americans use every day. As demand for these technologies increases, companies are looking beyond faster processors and exploring ways to make the facilities supporting them more efficient.

For Samsung, a possible deal with Modine could provide a stronger position in this expanding market.

Modine shares surge following acquisition report

News of Samsung‘s reported interest quickly attracted attention from investors.

Modine shares initially climbed 29% in extended trading following Bloomberg’s report. On Nov. 13, the stock closed at $135.66, representing a 27.9% increase from the previous trading session.

The rally pushed Modine’s market capitalization to approximately $7.2 billion, an increase of nearly $1.6 billion.

That figure represents the company’s stock market valuation rather than a confirmed acquisition price.

Before the report gained attention, Modine shares closed at $106.10 on Nov. 12. The subsequent increase illustrated how strongly investors responded to the possibility of Samsung entering the business.

However, shareholders could face uncertainty if negotiations collapse or another potential buyer enters the discussions.

For now, neither a finalized purchase agreement nor an official takeover price has been announced.

Why data center cooling is becoming a major AI opportunity

Although Modine may not be a familiar name to everyday consumers, its products serve an increasingly important part of the technology industry.

Data centers house powerful computers that process information for cloud platforms, online services and artificial intelligence applications. These machines generate substantial heat while operating, making cooling systems essential to keeping equipment functional.

As AI technology advances, the computing systems behind it require more electricity and produce additional heat. Companies must therefore invest in equipment that can maintain safe operating temperatures while controlling energy consumption.

The International Energy Agency estimates that cooling accounts for approximately 7% of electricity consumption at highly efficient large data centers. At less efficient facilities, that figure can exceed 30%.

Improving cooling technology could help operators reduce some of their operating expenses while making better use of available electricity.

For American consumers, the potential benefits could eventually extend to the digital services they use regularly. More efficient data centers could help technology companies manage the expenses associated with cloud storage, AI assistants and other online platforms.

Those savings could create opportunities for expanded services, additional computing capacity or more competitive pricing. However, lower operating expenses do not automatically mean customers will receive cheaper subscriptions or products.

Electricity demand is another important consideration. A June 2026 report from Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory estimated that data centers could account for approximately 11.8% of U.S. electricity consumption by 2030.

With demand expected to increase, cooling improvements could become an important part of efforts to manage the energy requirements of the expanding AI industry.

Modine’s financial growth helps explain Samsung’s interest

Modine’s recent financial performance offers another indication of why the company could attract attention from a major technology manufacturer.

In its Nov. 3 earnings announcement, Modine reported that data center sales reached $439.7 million during its second quarter, representing a 95% increase from the $225 million recorded during the same period a year earlier.

The data center division accounted for approximately 44% of the company’s total quarterly revenue of $994.4 million.

Modine also reported operating income of $61.2 million, an increase of 70% compared with the previous year.

The figures demonstrate how quickly its data center business has expanded alongside growing demand for AI-related infrastructure.

However, the company’s growth has also come with financial pressures. Its data center gross margin declined to 19.7%, down 4.7 percentage points from the previous year.

Higher expenses involving materials, components and tariffs contributed to the reduction.

For Samsung, these figures present an important consideration. Modine offers an established business in a growing industry, but expanding sales does not necessarily translate into stronger profit margins.

An acquisition would give Samsung an opportunity to expand its infrastructure operations, although the financial benefits would depend on how successfully it manages costs and integrates the business.

Samsung has already expanded into cooling technology

The reported interest in Modine would also build on Samsung’s previous efforts to strengthen its presence in the heating, ventilation and air conditioning industry.

In November 2025, Samsung completed its acquisition of FläktGroup, a European company specializing in heating, ventilation and cooling solutions.

The transaction expanded Samsung’s reach in commercial and industrial climate-control systems.

A potential Modine acquisition could take that strategy further by giving Samsung additional exposure to the specialized cooling equipment required by modern data centers.

Rather than concentrating primarily on smartphones, televisions and semiconductor technology, the company could become more involved in the infrastructure supporting the wider AI economy.

For investors, however, the distinction between a promising industry and a profitable acquisition remains important.

At Modine’s Nov. 12 closing price of $106.10, the stock was considerably below its Nov. 13 closing level of $135.66. If acquisition discussions collapse, shareholders could face the possibility of losing some of those gains.

The next major development will be whether Samsung makes a formal offer and what price it is prepared to pay.

For everyday consumers, the larger takeaway is that the future of AI depends on more than increasingly powerful computer chips. The companies developing the technology must also find better ways to manage the electricity, cooling systems and infrastructure required to keep digital services running.

Samsung’s reported interest in Modine highlights why those less visible parts of the technology industry could become increasingly important as AI adoption continues to grow.

Source : Bloomberg

data.title: Google says no evidence of widespread Gmail outage
data.description:
Gmail users flooded outage trackers with complaints on Tuesday, but Google says it isn’t seeing signs of a widespread problem.


The tech giant said on Tuesday, November 17, that it had found no evidence of a broad disruption to its popular email service, even as thousands of people reported trouble with their inboxes.


Thousands of users reported problems

By noon ET, outage tracking website Downdetector had logged more than 2,800 reports of issues with Gmail. Most users said they were having trouble receiving emails, while others reported problems getting into the service at all.

The complaints marked a second wave of reports. Downdetector data showed problems had already peaked around 2:40 p.m. ET on Monday before climbing again Tuesday morning.

For many people, Gmail is central to both work and personal life, so even scattered issues can cause headaches, from missed meeting invites to delayed verification codes and receipts.

What Google has said

A Google spokesperson told Rolling Out that the company was not seeing evidence of a broad Gmail service disruption. The spokesperson added that Google’s teams keep a close eye on service health and that real-time updates are always available on the Google Workspace Status Dashboard.

Google shared a similar message in a post on X from its News from Google account, encouraging users to check the dashboard for the latest information. The dashboard tracks the health of Gmail along with other Workspace apps, such as Google Drive and Google Meet.

As of 1:45 p.m. ET, the dashboard did not list any active Gmail disruptions.

The gap between user complaints and Google’s assessment is worth noting. Downdetector tracks reports submitted by users, so a spike signals that many people are noticing problems, but it doesn’t necessarily mean the service is down for everyone. Issues can also stem from individual accounts, devices, internet connections or the providers sending the messages.

A week of tech failures

The Gmail reports follow a rough stretch for some of the country’s biggest systems. In recent days, Americans have dealt with several major disruptions.

  1. A Microsoft Outlook outage last week left users without email for nearly 24 hours.
  2. A telecommunications failure prompted the Federal Aviation Administration to temporarily halt flights nationwide beginning Friday, November. 13.
  3. Chase customers reported login and account problems on Monday.
  4. Marriott’s website and app saw a spike in problem reports Tuesday morning, with hundreds of users reporting trouble with logins and reservations.

Taken together, the incidents have left many people frustrated with the reliability of the digital services they depend on every day. Still, there is no evidence that the Gmail complaints are connected to any of them.

We want to be clear that we aren’t currently seeing evidence of a broad Gmail service disruption, and you can always check real-time status on our Status Dashboard: https://t.co/hXJj1ijxrA

— News from Google (@NewsFromGoogle) November 17, 2026

What to do if Gmail isn’t working

If emails aren’t showing up, there are a few simple steps worth trying.

Start by checking the Google Workspace Status Dashboard to see whether the company has flagged a problem. If nothing is listed, try opening Gmail on a different device or switching between the app and a web browser, since issues sometimes affect one but not the other.

It’s also a good idea to check your spam and other folders, along with any filters you’ve set up, in case messages are being sorted somewhere unexpected. Sending a test email to yourself can show whether messages are coming through. Refreshing the page, updating the Gmail app or restarting your device can also help clear up minor glitches.

Anyone expecting time-sensitive emails may want to give contacts a heads-up or use another way to stay in touch until the issue clears up.

data.title: GTA 6 is breaking the real world in alarming ways
data.description:
Miami did not build Vice City. A studio in New York did, pixel by pixel, over more than a decade. Now the real city is absorbing the fictional one, and travelers are paying to see where the two overlap.


Searches for flights to Miami are surging worldwide, according to eSky Group, a travel agency based in Poland. Searches from Poland rose 215% between September 21 and November 15 compared with the same window a year earlier. Inquiries across the agency’s Latin American sites climbed roughly 200%.


The numbers behind Miami’s new pull

Package searches moved harder than flights alone. Combined flight and hotel searches for Miami rose 545% in Romania and 500% in Bulgaria.

Bookings followed. Miami package bookings climbed 56% over the past year, the agency said. Travelers paid about $1,350 a person for GTA 6 trips averaging eight nights.

That spread matters. The spike is loudest in markets far from Florida, where a Miami trip means a long haul and real money. These are not weekend drives from Orlando.

A city playing a character

Miami has met the moment by dressing the part. On November 18, the Miami Heat hosted the Milwaukee Bucks as Vice City, with a custom court, alternate uniforms and music pulled from the game’s world.

Concessions took names from fictional GTA restaurants including Burger Shot and Cluckin’ Bell. A Welcome to Vice City sign went up over the Kaseya Center. An allotment of the special jerseys sold out in roughly 90 minutes, the Associated Press reported.

The downtown nightclub E11even has taken on the look and name of the game’s copycat venue, Nine1nine, through December 6. Rockstar is staging its own music festival in Wynwood on November 21.

Why this GTA surge behaves differently

Film and television have redirected tourism for decades. A location appears for 90 minutes, viewers recognize it, bookings tick up.

Marcin Starkowski, group PR manager at eSky.com, framed the difference as time spent. GTA players live inside a virtual city for dozens of hours, absorbing its architecture, its landmarks and its mood before ever seeing a real street. By the time they land, the place already feels familiar.

That changes what a visitor wants. A film tourist hunts for a single facade. A player arrives with a mental map.

The part nobody is pricing in

Miami is collecting revenue from an identity it did not author and does not control. The jerseys, the club rebrand, the festival weekend all trace back to a product owned by a private company.

Rockstar can redirect that attention whenever it chooses. The GTA series has used other cities before, and nothing obligates it to keep Miami in the spotlight. A city leaning into a borrowed persona inherits a timeline it cannot set.

For now the flights are filling. Whether that holds past the first wave of players is a question the booking data will answer long before anyone in Miami does.

data.title: Experts Warn Another Internet Outage Could Lock You Out Next
data.description:
A wave of crashes at Microsoft, Apple, JPMorgan Chase and the airlines has specialists urging Americans to protect their money, files and holiday travel before the next failure hits


A run of technology failures this month has left Americans staring at error screens, and cybersecurity experts say the stumbles are less a fluke than a preview.


Since the start of November, a sweeping Microsoft cloud outage has disrupted businesses, health care providers and banks. The Federal Aviation Administration is still investigating a telecommunications breakdown that triggered a nationwide ground stop last Friday. On Monday, thousands of customers reported trouble getting into their online bank accounts, a problem JPMorgan Chase later blamed on a temporary software glitch. United Airlines said a computer issue delayed departing flights that same day, and on Tuesday, Apple said an internal update knocked the App Store and other services offline.

The pileup has fueled online chatter about coordinated attacks and planned blackouts. Experts say the reality is more ordinary, and in some ways more unsettling.

What’s Really Behind the Outage Wave

Michael Chapple, a professor of IT, analytics and operations at the University of Notre Dame, said there is no reason to believe the country is under a cyberattack. He called the timing of the failures largely coincidental but said they expose real weaknesses in the nation’s technology infrastructure, and that more incidents are likely as society leans harder on complicated systems.

Part of the problem is concentration. Feng Li, associate dean for research and innovation at Bayes Business School at City St George’s, University of London, noted that so many services run on the same underlying systems that switching from a bank’s app to its website may not help. A breakdown at one bank, he added, can also delay payments to customers at another.

First, Confirm It’s Not Just You

When an app freezes or a site won’t load, first figure out whether the trouble is widespread. Downdetector compiles user reports of disrupted services, though Kayne McGladrey, a security expert and senior member of the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, cautioned that its numbers can swell when anxious users pile on during high-profile events.

Sites such as Is It Down Right Now test availability directly, and many companies publish their own real-time status pages. During Tuesday’s disruption, Apple’s System Status page showed whether the App Store was working.

Back Up Your Digital Life

Many Outlook users lost access to their inboxes during the Microsoft failure, a reminder that contacts and documents can become unreachable at the worst moment. Chapple recommends synchronization tools that keep working copies across several devices, such as Google Drive synced to a personal computer, so work can continue even when a provider fails.

Protect Your Money When Banks Go Offline

For working families, a frozen bank app can mean a missed ride, a stalled bill payment or a grocery run cut short. Li suggests carrying a backup card from a different bank. McGladrey goes further, keeping two to four weeks of cash in small bills and spreading his money across institutions and payment types, including a credit card from another issuer, a debit card and, ideally, a credit union account.

Deposits are not the main danger, he said, since FDIC-insured accounts are protected up to $250,000. Scammers are. Fake texts claiming an account has been locked tend to spike during outages, so any unsolicited message about your finances should be treated as hostile. If you need money immediately, visit a branch or an ATM. Otherwise, wait, since these incidents usually clear the same day, and do not resubmit transfers that may already be processing.

Chapple also advises keeping bank security features switched on and using multifactor authentication so unusual activity stands out quickly.

Plan Ahead for Holiday Travel

With technical delays repeatedly hitting airlines this month, experts urge travelers to build in flexibility. Li recommends turning on airline alerts and leaving extra time for fixed-date commitments. McGladrey suggests buffer days around important trips, knowing your rebooking options and insuring expensive nonrefundable tickets. Chapple suggests mapping out alternatives, such as a rental car or a train, since those who react fastest avoid the longest lines.

Even solid preparation will not erase every inconvenience, Chapple acknowledged. Sometimes the only option is turning to other tasks for a few hours.

Li argues the burden should not fall on consumers alone. Regulators, he said, should gather evidence from operators, investigate what went wrong, publish their findings, confirm that backup systems work in practice and tighten rules where needed to prevent a repeat.

Source: HUFFPOST

data.title: Game Awards 2026: Who is nominated and who got left out?
data.description:
The nominees for The Game Awards 2026 are out, and Grand Theft Auto VI leads the way with eight nominations, including Game of the Year, even though it does not release until Thursday, Nov. 19. Host Geoff Keighley revealed the lists in a livestream today. The ceremony takes place Dec. 10 at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles.


Who are the Game of the Year nominees?

The six nominees are 007 First Light, Control Resonant, Grand Theft Auto VI, Phantom Blade Zero, Resident Evil Requiem and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Last year’s winner was Clair Obscur: Expedition 33.


What did GTA 6 earn?

Besides Game of the Year, it is nominated for Best Game Direction, Best Narrative, Best Art Direction, Best Score and Music, Best Audio Design, Best Action/Adventure and Best Performance for Manni L. Perez. The Performance nod confirms Perez plays Lucia. Variety counts eight nominations, while a Forbes list shows fewer categories, so counts differ by outlet.

Is GTA 6 eligible?

Yes. The eligibility window ends Friday, Nov. 20, and the award releases before that. Some fans suggested the show moved its dates to fit the game. Keighley rejected that and said the calendar is the same every year. Forbes notes the game has no reviews yet, so some voters may have chosen it sight unseen.

Who else is nominated?

Best Ongoing includes Arc Raiders, Final Fantasy XIV, Fortnite, No Man’s Sky and The Witcher 3. Most Anticipated includes Fable, Final Fantasy VII Revelation, God of War Laufey, Resident Evil Veronica and The Witcher 4. Content Creator of the Year includes IShowSpeed, CDawg, Cellbit, LilSimsie and OhnePixel.

Best Multiplayer features Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, Gears of War: E-Day, Marathon and others.

How are winners picked?

A global jury of more than 100 media outlets and creators chooses nominees, and winners come from a mix of jury and fan votes. Fans can vote at TheGameAwards.com. The show will stream on more platforms than ever, including Disney+, Roblox, YouTube, Twitch, Steam and TikTok Live.

What is not confirmed?

The nomination count for GTA 6 varies by source, and Variety’s story names Grand Theft Auto IV in one line, which looks like a typo. A claim that the cost $2 billion is a rumor. Winners are not decided until Dec. 10.

data.title: GTA 6 vs. your job: Fans are choosing the game
data.description:
Grand Theft Auto VI arrives at midnight Thursday, Nov. 19, and many fans have rearranged work and home life to play from the first minute. It is the franchise’s first new game in more than a decade, and the release has been delayed twice, from 2025 to May 2026 and then to November.


How are fans preparing?

Ciara Singleton, who manages an Airbnb, is weighing a costume party with several TVs and consoles or a theater screening on a friend’s projector. Thomas Gaskins, a father of two teens, took Nov. 19 and 20 off and plans to play until 5 a.m. Dakota Eldridge, an event planner in Kentucky, will take 10 days off while keeping up meal prep and gym sessions.


Software engineer Malcolm Bixby is taking two weeks off and built a spreadsheet for play, sleep and meals. In Texas, Kelsey Rogers got time off after telling her boss the reason, and he said he was also taking days off. She expects her company may not run for two or three days.

Are employers getting involved?

An Army battalion at Fort Stewart, Georgia, is reportedly offering four days off tied to the release in exchange for reenlisting for two to six years. IGN reported that Logitech is giving employees the day off, and its CEO said it is time to retire the idea that gaming is a waste of time.

What is the game about?

Players return to Vice City, a fictional city based on Miami, first seen in 2002. For the first time, players can switch between a male and a female lead, Jason, a former soldier, and Lucia, who has a long rap sheet. Singleton wore a Lucia costume in Miami over Halloween and said strangers recognized her.

What do the numbers show?

One report says the game passed $1 billion in sales a week before release, which would top the domestic box office of the latest Spider-Man film. Analysts estimate the cost above $1 billion, though Take-Two has not given a figure. Take-Two’s CEO called it expensive.

Why does the game resonate?

An Rochester Institute of Technology professor says it offers a funhouse mirror view of America, with references to music, TV and movies that are instantly recognizable.

Are some players trying to play early?

Some Xbox users are changing their console location to a time zone where the game unlocks first, since New Zealand gets it earliest. That workaround is unverified, and the platform terms may not allow it.

What is not confirmed?

The $1 billion cost is an estimate, and the sales milestone comes from one report. The first official sales figures are expected after launch. Whether the Army offer applies across units was not detailed.

data.title: Microsoft reveals 3 causes behind massive Outlook outage
data.description:
Microsoft is finally explaining what went wrong during last week’s massive Outlook outage, which left people around the world struggling to use the popular email service across two full workdays. On Monday, November 16, a company executive apologized for the disruption in a lengthy social media post and laid out a chain of problems that combined to knock the platform offline, ABC News reported.


Charles Lamanna, Microsoft’s executive vice president of Copilot, Agents and Platform, said a hidden software defect, a spike in demand and reduced server capacity all played a role in the breakdown.


A widespread disruption

The outage rippled across a wide range of industries. Businesses, government offices, schools and health care providers all reported communication problems as the email service faltered.

Other Microsoft platforms, including Teams and Xbox Live, were also affected for hours across North America, leaving many workers unable to reach colleagues or clients during the busiest part of the week.

The company had previously said the outage was not caused by a hack and that its AI agents were not responsible.

The 3 causes behind the outage

Lamanna identified three main issues that worked together to bring Outlook down.

The first was a hidden defect that had been lying dormant in the system. Under certain conditions, the bug caused servers to become overwhelmed and stop responding. According to Lamanna, the flaw came from a fix that Microsoft had prepared specifically for its Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers back in July.

The second cause was a sudden surge in traffic hitting that networking gateway, which put added pressure on the system.

The third factor was reduced server capacity. Lamanna noted that this reduction would not have caused any problems by itself, but it became significant when combined with the other two issues.

How the problems combined

When the increased traffic met the reduced capacity, the networking gateway triggered the bug that had been introduced months earlier. Requests then began piling up until the servers stopped responding altogether.

The timing made matters worse. The failure struck during the peak window of internet traffic in the United States, when demand for email and workplace tools is at its highest.

Why recovery took so long

Many users were frustrated by how long it took for service to return to normal. Lamanna explained that recovery was slower than usual because of the way the system came back online.

As servers were restored, they were immediately flooded by the backlog of waiting traffic. That sudden rush overwhelmed them again, causing them to become unresponsive and repeating the cycle. Breaking that loop took additional time, extending the outage well beyond what customers might typically expect.

Microsoft says it’s sorry

In his update, Lamanna offered a sincere apology on behalf of the company. He said Microsoft deeply regrets the impact on its customers and recognizes how much the outage interfered with their normal business operations.

The explanation offers rare insight into how a single dormant bug can spiral into a global disruption when several pressures hit at once.

What it means for users

For the millions of people who depend on Outlook and Teams every day, the outage served as a reminder of how much modern work relies on a handful of digital platforms. When those services go dark, entire offices, classrooms and hospitals can feel the effects within minutes.

The incident also comes during a period of significant change at Microsoft, which recently offered buyouts to 60,000 employees as its spending on artificial intelligence continues to grow.

Microsoft has not said whether it will make further changes to prevent a similar outage, but the detailed breakdown suggests the company is working to rebuild trust with frustrated customers.

This story was originally reported by ABC News.
